extracted.intended_audience: EPA rulemakers and policy staff; environmental advocates, attorneys, and stakeholders submitting or reviewing notice-and-comment submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Legal/technical public comments on EPA's proposed NESHAP (40 C.F.R. Part 63) for the Oil and Natural Gas sector, addressing required residual risk review under CAA §112(f)(2) and the eight-year MACT review under §112(d)(6) and urging stronger standards and procedures. The document articulates statutory obligations, data and analysis expectations, control and monitoring requirements, and health-protective policy choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residual risk assessment under CAA §112(f)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must assess the health risk that remains with the standards in place and decide whether additional emission reductions are needed to reach an acceptable level of risk and to provide an 'ample margin of safety for public health' in local communities near these sources. (42 U.S.C. § 7412(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment must identify an acceptable or 'safe' level of risk, consider the communities affected, the greater risk to children, and cumulative impacts; must not focus primarily on cost. EPA must explain its analysis and set limits to provide the ample margin of safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and address all HAP emissions and emission points
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must assess and regulate all hazardous air pollutant (HAP) emissions from the Oil and Gas source categories, including emission points not previously regulated under the original MACT (e.g., wastewater pits and impoundments, well pads, well completions, fugitive toxic air emissions, produced water tanks, storage vessels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 112(f)(2) requires a complete rulemaking for the entire source category; omission of emission points violates the statute. EPA must set MACT limits for previously uncontrolled emission points and cannot limit the review to only previously regulated points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of actual measured emissions data (not only NEI estimates)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should collect and use actual emission test data rather than relying on the National Emissions Inventory (NEI) estimates as the starting point for the risk assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NEI (2005) is outdated and lacks data for the majority of facilities; EPA must justify the use of NEI or obtain stack/point test data (CAA §114 authority) to ensure representative, reliable inputs. EPA must account for uncertainty when using estimates and compare estimates to test data where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include hydrogen sulfide and particulate matter in analysis and controls
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must regulate significant air pollutants emitted by oil and gas, including hydrogen sulfide (H2S) and particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: H2S is highly toxic and found in many gas deposits; it should be listed under §112 or regulated under §111 until listed. PM emissions occur throughout drilling and transport; cost-effective controls (dust suppression, speed limits, road planning) are available and should be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider multipathway exposures and add to inhalation risk
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must adequately address non-inhalation or 'multipathway' risks (ingestion, dermal) and include multipathway risk in overall risk determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's multipathway analysis must not be arbitrary; it must include all relevant HAPs, assess risk based on allowable emissions, and add multipathway risks to inhalation risks where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for malfunctions and violations in risk assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must not ignore risks from malfunctions, exceedances, or violations; these events should be considered in assessing the full cancer and chronic non-cancer health risk from the source category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA should remove start-up, shutdown, and malfunction (SSM) exemptions and must not promulgate an 'affirmative defense' for malfunctions; the residual risk assessment must include malfunction-related exposures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect the most-exposed individual and fence-line exposures
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must assess cancer and chronic risk exposure for the maximum exposed person at the fence line and ensure standards protect the most-exposed individual and communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk determinations and acceptable-risk decisions must be based on protecting the most-exposed person rather than averaging exposure across larger populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate early life vulnerability and prenatal susceptibility
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must include early life vulnerability in cancer assessments, account for increased prenatal susceptibility to carcinogens, and generally consider heightened sensitivity of children and fetuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow California OEHHA child-protective scientific approach; consider using additional uncertainty factors (e.g., a 10-fold factor) at appropriate steps to protect children and pregnant women.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess cumulative impacts and environmental justice concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must adequately assess cumulative impacts of exposure to this source category in combination with other HAP emissions and recognize socioeconomic disparity in health risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider communities facing multiple sources of pollution, vulnerable subpopulations, and the principle of environmental justice when determining acceptability and ample margin of safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update acceptable cancer-risk benchmark and justify standard
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should not rely uncritically on the outdated presumption that 100-in-1 million lifetime cancer risk is acceptable; it must re-evaluate and possibly lower the benchmark (commenters urge protection from cancer risk above 1-in-1 million).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must provide a reasoned explanation for its acceptability threshold, consider evolving science and values, and has authority to adopt more protective presumptions under §112(f)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine and explain emission reductions needed for an 'ample margin of safety'
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must assess the level of emissions reductions required to provide an 'ample' margin of safety (i.e., more than a bare minimum) and explain that analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'ample margin' determination must consider full health threats to vulnerable populations, cumulative impacts, and a range of control options; cost considerations cannot override the legal duty to protect public health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set numerical emission limits for every HAP emitted
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's proposal must set a numerical emission limit for every HAP emitted by the source category to satisfy §112(d)(2)-(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MACT standards should reflect emission levels achieved by best performing sources for each HAP; numeric limits are needed rather than partial or categorical controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set MACT floors and consider beyond-the-floor standards based on current best performers
rubrics_metrics.description: For final rules EPA must determine MACT standards based on emissions performance and control technologies achieved by or available to the industry today and consider all practices/processes/technologies that can achieve greater HAP reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on 1999 data; consider state/local programs, consent decrees, BACT determinations, Natural Gas Star, and other evidence of higher-performing controls. Update MACT floors and evaluate beyond-the-floor options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengthen LDAR and reduce leak detection thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must reduce leak detection and repair (LDAR) thresholds (supporting reduction for valves at natural gas plants from 10,000 to 500 ppm) and apply similarly stringent thresholds to other equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA should not allow 2% of equipment to leak indefinitely; adopt more stringent LDAR programs as implemented in California air districts and regulatory settlements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require higher control efficiency (98–99%) for storage vessels and dehydrators
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must require at least 98–99% control efficiency for storage vessels and dehydrators rather than the 95% level proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdictions such as Wyoming already require higher efficiencies; EPA should match achievable levels demonstrated elsewhere and in enforcement cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control produced water tanks and eliminate or cover pits/impoundments
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must regulate air pollution from produced water tanks and ponds; consider eliminating open pits and requiring that produced water be kept in tanks or require covers for pits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wyoming mandates 98% control for new produced water tanks; controls reduce air emissions and have co-benefits for preventing groundwater contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require periodic monitoring, electronic reporting, and public data access
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should require periodic monitoring (including electronic reporting), recordkeeping, and reporting, and ensure monitoring data are publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic reporting facilitates transparency and enforcement; combustion-control device testing requirements should be clear and robust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove SSM exemptions and reject affirmative defense for malfunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters support removal of start-up, shut-down, and malfunction exemptions as required by the Clean Air Act and oppose EPA's proposed affirmative defense for malfunctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SSM exemptions undermine protective standards; affirmative defenses effectively excuse violations and are unlawful in this context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct the required eight-year MACT review without delay
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must perform the §112(d)(6) eight-year MACT review and update existing §112(d) standards based on developments since the last rulemaking; EPA may not refuse or postpone the required review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review must satisfy §§112(d)(2)-(3) and update MACT floors and beyond-the-floor analyses where warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct cost and benefit analyses to reflect true cost-effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's analyses of control costs and cost-effectiveness, as well as cost-benefit analyses, must not overstate costs or underestimate benefits; corrected analyses may support more stringent standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-evaluate assumptions and methodologies; properly accounting for benefits and accurate costs could justify stronger controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and tightly limit waivers/exceptions (e.g., 'predicated' pneumatic waiver)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must not include vague exceptions (such as allowing operators to avoid low-bleed or no-bleed pneumatic devices when their use is not 'predicated' without defining 'predicated').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If waivers are appropriate, EPA must precisely define circumstances, allow public comment, and subject exemptions to challenge to avoid undermining the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require MACT standards and floors for small glycol dehydrators and storage vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must properly calculate and set MACT limits under §112(d)(2)-(3) for small glycol dehydrators and previously uncontrolled storage vessels, including determining MACT floors for all HAPs and conducting updated beyond-the-floor analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on incomplete or outdated data; set numeric limits for these newly controlled emission points and analyze achievable controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate the 1‑ton benzene allowance and tighten benzene limits for area sources
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should remove the 1-ton benzene allowance for glycol dehydrators and reduce benzene limits for glycol dehydrator area sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support is expressed for EPA's proposed removal of the 1-ton allowance, but commenters urge stronger, health-protective benzene limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for emissions produced by control devices themselves
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must consider that control devices can generate additional pollutants and ensure emissions from control devices are included in emissions inventories and risk assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to account for control-device emissions could underestimate total HAP releases; testing should capture emissions 'created by control devices.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure data representativeness and account for industry changes (shale/fracturing)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must use up-to-date, representative data that reflect rapid industry changes (e.g., shale gas, hydraulic fracturing) and explain why any data used are appropriate substitutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 2005 NEI data are outdated; EPA must justify reliance on estimates or obtain newer measurements and account for uncertainty arising from limited facility coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce acute and chronic non-cancer risks to acceptable levels
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must evaluate and reduce acute health risks (where EPA's analysis found levels 5–9 times the threshold) and chronic non-cancer health risks identified in the risk review that are unacceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA must justify any decision not to require reductions below acute thresholds and must recognize and act upon chronic non-cancer risks.
